status.main_product: Digital network and SaaS solutions for trade finance operations
status.scope_reason: The company builds and operates Global Trade Konnect (GTK) and Konsole, which are multi-bank platforms and digital networks designed for managing and automating trade finance instruments like letters of credit and guarantees.
status.evidence: According to Komgo's official product updates and profiles, the company provides multi-bank SaaS applications and a secure digital network explicitly built for managing trade finance workflows and connecting corporates with financial institutions.

claims.claim: Independent verification shows that Crédit Agricole CIB utilizes Komgo's multibank integration layer to route and execute structured digital workflows for documentary credits, standby letters of credit, bank guarantees, and collections.

The company reports that its Global Trade Konnect application, launched in April 2025, utilizes integrated artificial intelligence to compare transaction data, extract info from draft invoices, and automate document checking.
A partnership established by the company with Complidata in 2025 adds AI-assisted document checking capabilities focused directly on trade document accuracy.
claims.note: partnership with Complidata in 2025

claims.claim: The company reports that its platform integrates directly with the SWIFT network using its proprietary Swift key via Swift's NOSU solution, and it supports the commercialized ICC-Swift API standards for bank guarantees.

Komgo collaborated with FIATA to implement the electronic forwarder's bill of lading (eFBL) data standard using its blockchain-based Trakk solution to allow the secure tracking and authentication of digital shipping documents.

Komgo reports that its infrastructure utilizes a secure cloud-native SaaS deployment model delivering decentralized digital connectivity via the Konsole multi-bank network. The architecture is underpinned by an enterprise Ethereum distributed ledger technology framework (built on Quorum) featuring a proprietary document transfer mechanism called Kite that supports secure peer-to-peer data validation and privacy by design.
claims.source: Consensys case study (https://consensys.io/blockchain-use-cases/finance/komgo) and Komgo documentation outlining Quorum and Kite framework.

claims.claim: The company reports offering extensive open API integration capability (including compliance with ICC-SWIFT API standards) to connect seamlessly with banks' back-office core systems, corporate ERP, and TMS solutions, processing nearly one billion dollars in financial transactions across its network daily.
claims.source: Komgo FAQ (https://www.komgo.io/faq) confirming $1 billion in daily transaction value and industry standard alignment with ICC-Swift API specifications.

claims.claim: The company reports the rollout of Global Trade Konnect (GTK) in April 2025, which serves as its consolidated SaaS application merging multi-bank trade finance workflows with embedded artificial intelligence tools including an LC Creation Agent, Digital Reporting Assistant, and Smart Clause Checker.
claims.source: Komgo Newsroom announcements from April 2025 regarding the flagship launch of Global Trade Konnect (GTK) along with its feature documentation outlining embedded generative AI assistants (https://www.komgo.io/newsroom/introducing-gtk-future-of-digital-guarantee-and-trade-finance-management).

claims.claim: In September 2026, the company announced a collaboration with Crédit Agricole CIB to integrate AI-powered capabilities into the bank's Optimtrade digital trade finance portal.
claims.source: Official press release published on Komgo Newsroom on September 24, 2026, titled 'Crédit Agricole CIB and Komgo collaborate to bring AI-powered capabilities to Optimtrade' (https://komgo.io).

claims.claim: Komgo reports that its multibank trade finance platform connects more than 300 corporates and financial institutions across 50 countries, with specific shareholders and users including global entities such as BNP Paribas, Citibank, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), Crédit Agricole CIB, TotalEnergies, Shell, Gunvor, and Koch Supply & Trading.
claims.source: Komgo corporate info page and ecosystem updates detailing network size of over 300 corporates and financial institutions across 50 countries, as well as founding shareholder records (https://www.komgo.io/about).

claims.claim: Publicly announced customer deployments include ANDRITZ deploying Komgo's Global Trade Konnect (GTK) solution across 40 countries to digitalize communications with 30+ financing partners, Standard Chartered executing its first ICC-SWIFT API standards bank guarantee transaction via Komgo, and case studies highlighting active utilization by Siemens Healthineers, Baker Hughes, Société Générale, and DBS Bank.
